text:
maria_support: Customer opened an urgent case — intermittent mTLS handshake failures to Private control plane after they pressed a new egress NAT appliance yesterday. Customers see lots of TLS alerts and timeouts.

jon_sre: Can you drop the minimal repro logs and a pcap? do we have trace ids from the failed requests?

maria_support: TraceID=rp-8f3b2a. Attached small pcap snippet from customer's tcpdump (they redacted IPs). Key bits: clienthello then immediate TLS Alert(20): handshake_failure or TCP RST. They also included the app logs: `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` in a couple of cases.

lee_infra: quick look — the pcap shows ClientHello with SNI present sometimes and absent other times. When SNI is present we get a normal ServerHello; when absent we see `Alert: handshake_failure` from our control plane and then the customer NAT resets. smells like a TLS-inspection device randomly stripping SNI or truncating ClientHello due to packet fragmentation.

anya_security: also note several ClientHello include TLS1.3 with ESNI/0x? extensions and we see OCSP stapling requests timing out towards the control plane. Middlebox could be intercepting or failing to forward full ClientHello.

maria_support: customer confirms they rolled NAT+TLS-inspect appliance at 02:00 UTC and issues started immediately after. They test directly from a jump host (bypassing appliance) and everything works.

jon_sre: can customer reproduce with these quick commands? ask them to run both:
```
# openssl test (shows handshake details)
openssl s_client -connect controlplane.private.redwood:443 -servername controlplane.private.redwood -cert client.crt -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -tls1_2 -msg
```
and
```
# curl test (mTLS)
curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://controlplane.private.redwood/api/v1/ping
```
If they see success when bypassing appliance but fail through it, it's definitely their egress path.

maria_support: customer ran both. Via appliance: openssl output ends with `<<< TLS 1.2 ALERT: Handshake Failure` and `write:errno=104` (connection reset). Direct jump-host -> success. They also reported one case where forcing `-tls1_2` helped while TLS1.3 failed more often.

lee_infra: that matches a TLS middlebox that can't handle TLS1.3 extensions or large ClientHello sizes (client cert chain + extensions). They might be reassembling wrongly and sending a truncated ClientHello to our control plane. Two mitigation paths: ask customer to enable TLS passthrough for control plane IPs / disable TLS inspection for those destinations OR upgrade the inspection device config to support TLS1.3 / large ClientHello reassembly.

anya_security: also verify that the customer's firewall/NAT preserves the full client certificate chain and client hello SNI. Some appliances drop intermediate certs or rewrite TLS metadata which breaks mTLS. Recommend they check for any policy that strips `certificateRequest` or modifies `ClientHello` extensions.

maria_support: I've drafted a short repro snippet and recommended steps; sending to customer now with suggested temporary workaround (egress allowlist + TLS passthrough). Also asked for a fresh pcap with `-s 0 -w` of both sides and `tcpdump -nnvvXS` including the first failing handshake.

jon_sre: if they can share the full pcap we can confirm if our control plane actually sent `Alert` or if the reset is network-side. If it's our Alert it's different; so far it looks like the control plane sees a malformed ClientHello and sends `handshake_failure`.

deploy-bot: note: We pushed a minor control plane logging change (prod) to add `client_hello_size` in TLS logs — should help correlate. Rolling forward. :hammer_and_wrench:

maria_support: customer did an interim test — they added our control plane CIDR to their egress passthrough list and the failures dropped to zero in 15m.

lee_infra: good signal. Final recommendation to customer: 1) add Redwood Private control plane IP ranges to egress allowlist and configure TLS passthrough (no TLS inspection). 2) ensure their NAT preserves SNI and client cert chain (no cert chain truncation). 3) upgrade TLS-inspection device or enable TLS1.3-friendly parsing/reassembly. 4) if they must inspect, configure an explicit proxy that terminates and re-issues client certs with correct trust chain (NOT recommended for mTLS).

anya_security: also ask them to rotate client certs if any were fetched while device was misbehaving — out of abundance of caution.

maria_support: I'll close the escalation once they confirm full stability for 24h. adding KB snippet to the case with the `openssl` and `curl` commands + sample tcpdump lines and the suggested firewall rule template. cc @jon_sre for follow up in case they re-open. :white_check_mark:

jon_sre: thanks — good root cause: TLS-inspection/NAT appliance interfering with ClientHello (SNI/hello size/fragmentation), temporary resolution via egress allowlist + TLS passthrough. Will keep the new logging on to catch any future similar patterns.

maria_support: case updated: Case# RI-2026-384 — included pcap excerpts, traceID, recommended actions.

jon_sre: 👍
